rules.text: An empty or stale worker lease may be acquired; an active lease held by another owner returns exact error BUSY without mutation.
renew and release require both the current owner identity and exact token; mismatch returns NOT_OWNER without mutation.
Expiry uses the injected virtual clock. The lease is stale when clock.now() >= expiresAt; renew or release of that unreclaimed stale record returns STALE.
A valid renew sets expiresAt to clock.now()+ttl. A valid release removes the lease record completely.
Reclaiming a stale lease creates a fresh token. The former token cannot mutate the reclaimed active lease, even when the same owner reacquires it.
Trace is append-only and copied on read. Each operation emits exactly one of acquire, reclaim, renew, release, deny after its decision, in call order.

callableSurface.ownership: The factory owns worker lease state, token sequencing and trace; caller owns the read-only virtual clock.

transitions: stale acquire -> active with fresh token
valid renew -> active with new expiry

eventOrdering: one trace event is appended after each decision
failed operations append deny and do not mutate
reclaim replaces stale ownership before reclaim is observed
valid release removes state before release/unlock is observed
abortErrorPrecedence: Expiry is evaluated before owner/token validation on the current record. After reclaim, validation applies to the new active owner/token, so any former token is NOT_OWNER.

identityMutation.inputs: keys, owner identities, tokens and virtual clock are read only
identityMutation.tokens: every successful fresh acquisition/reclaim gets a new token
identityMutation.trace: trace returns a new array with new event objects
